definition: In computer science and machine learning, Cellular Neural Networks (CNN) or Cellular Nonlinear Networks (CNN) are a parallel computing paradigm similar to neural networks, with the difference that communication is allowed between neighbouring units only.
details: Typical applications include image processing, analyzing 3D surfaces, solving partial differential equations, reducing non-visual problems to geometric maps, modelling biological vision and other sensory-motor organs. CNN is not to be confused with convolutional neural networks (also colloquially called CNN).

explainer.lead: A cellular neural network is a parallel computing architecture made of many units that communicate only with their neighbours. This local structure makes it useful for tasks such as image processing, analysing 3D surfaces and modelling biological vision.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a grid of children solving a puzzle together, but each child may talk only to the children sitting directly nearby. Everyone works at the same time, and their small local exchanges gradually produce an answer for the whole grid. This is the basic idea behind a cellular neural network.
tiers.practitioner: Cellular neural networks can be applied to image processing, 3D-surface analysis, partial differential equations and geometric formulations of non-visual problems. Their defining design constraint is that each unit communicates only with neighbouring units, while computation proceeds in parallel. Do not confuse the CNN abbreviation here with convolutional neural networks.
tiers.paperLevel: A Cellular Neural Network, also called a Cellular Nonlinear Network, is a parallel computing paradigm in which communication is restricted to neighbouring units. It otherwise resembles a neural-network architecture and supports both linear and nonlinear formulations under the CNN name. Applications include image processing, 3D-surface analysis, partial differential equations, geometric maps and models of biological sensory-motor systems.

explainer.example: In an image-processing task, each unit can handle a local part of the image and exchange information with units handling neighbouring parts. The units work in parallel, so local changes can be coordinated across the image without direct communication between distant units.

usedIn.name: Partial differential equations

usedIn.name: Biological vision modelling
usedIn.detail: Models biological vision and other sensory-motor organs.

components.name: Computing units
components.detail: Individual units perform computation in parallel, similarly to units in other neural networks.

components.name: Neighbourhood connections
components.detail: Communication links allow each unit to exchange information only with neighbouring units.

components.name: Parallel computation
components.detail: The units operate together rather than relying on a single sequence of centralised calculations.

flow: A problem is represented across the network's computing units.
Each unit computes while exchanging information only with its neighbours.
These local interactions run in parallel across the network.
The resulting network state provides the processed result.
explainer.whyItMatters: It shows how parallel computation can be organised through local communication alone, with uses ranging from image processing to differential equations and biological modelling.
